ai_summary:
Today's system metrics illustrate a stark operational disparity across the national network, shaped by high renewable availability in the north alongside acute transmission export limitations. Total GB wind output currently reaches 13.7 GW, underpinned by an estimated Scottish wind output of 5.0 GW, which represents 49.5% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This strong renewable volume has driven Scottish carbon intensity down to 0 gCO2/kWh, contrasting sharply with the GB-wide carbon intensity of 123 gCO2/kWh.

However, structural grid bottlenecks prevent this clean power from flowing smoothly to primary demand centres. As a consequence, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has mounted to 42586.6 MWh, generating a substantial constraint cost of about £1,078,158 paid to balance the network. To compensate for this stranded clean electricity, flexible thermal assets were dispatched elsewhere, resulting in an estimated gas burned elsewhere to replace it of 8091454.0 m3. This intervention released an additional 14905.3 tonnes CO2 into the atmosphere. The resulting figures emphasize the simultaneous financial and environmental costs of current grid congestion, highlighting how transmission barriers undermine zero-carbon generation and enforce fossil reliance.
